text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- The Serbian parliament will hold its regular session on Tuesday, December 17 and has a number of legal acts proposed by the government on its agenda.
- The Serbian government adopts its 1997 draft budget at 14.060 billion dinars ($2.74 billion).
- Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini visits Belgrade today.

- The firm Cer of Cacak signed a $1 million agreement with the Chinese company Jinkai from Nanjing on the delivery of equipment for processing and drying of vegetables. The agreement comes within the scope of the one billion dollar Yugoslav-Chinese barter deal.

- The private sector share in Yugoslavia's economy reached 30.2 percent in the first six months of 1996, the Yugoslav chamber of commerce said. The sector employs 11.4 percent of Yugoslavia's total workforce.

- The National Bank of Yugoslavia is trying to maintain a stable dinar rate said there should be no devaluation of the domestic currency, although numerous economic problems influence the rate, said Deputy Governor of the central bank Bozidar Gazivoda.
- Protests continue in Belgrade, Nis, Kragujevac and other towns of Serbia over annullment of election results.
- Over 40,000 students continue protest in Belgrade, their collegues in Novi Sad and Nis protest also.
- Radio Television Serbia direcotr Dragoljub Milanovic sends film editor Mladen Popovic on compulsory leave for taking part in Belgrade demonstrations.
- Independent student movement, which is opposed to students missing classes, calls Belgrade student protest 1996 initiative board for a meeting.
- The Serbian agrarian sector could export produce to the value of $1.5 billion in 1997, said Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Nedeljko Sipovac.

- The federal and republican prime ministers met reprsentatives of the national bank of Yugoslavia and the chamber of commerce to discuss the 1997 monetary policy which is aimed at maintaining stability of the domestic currency and prices.
